source.title: Controlling Polar Exposure to Delay Memorization in Diffusion Models
source.authors: Xuan-Chen Wang; Heng Wang; Wei-Dong Cai

record.tranche_reason: Tests optimizer effects on the quality-to-copying interval in diffusion models, a generative setting outside the listed supervised-label versions.
record.gate_note: The study measures generative quality and detected training-image copying, not training error versus held-out error on natural labels. Its random-feature population-prediction and fluctuation clocks are theoretical or diagnostic results and do not establish any listed version.
record.test_reason: The study measures diffusion sample quality, detected training-image copying, and optimizer-dependent learning clocks. None measures V1–V8: copying is not random-label fitting or removal-based example memorization, and generative FID is not the classifier or language-model performance comparison specified by V4. The record's T3 classification is therefore incorrect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Under aligned fixed-feature assumptions and a positive residual margin, finite polar exposure restores a dataset-size-dependent memorization delay. Empirically, QGD preserves Muon's early quality arrival and improves its later quality–copying tradeoff; hard switching delays copying more strongly. CBS controls joint release and detector-budget violation for the specified detector, without guaranteeing absence of undetected copying.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains diffusion denoisers and evaluates sample quality and detected copying, rather than testing supervised classification networks, random labels, or held-out label accuracy.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer and post-gate exposure control; dataset size; controller settings and probe cadence.

fits_no_version.finding: Relative to continued Muon, QGD increases the observed quality-to-copying interval from 20.0 to 166.4 thousand updates at n=2,000 and from 84.0 to 348.0 thousand at n=10,000. Common-checkpoint detected copying falls from 16.10% to 3.88% and from 12.37% to 2.99%, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested diffusion setup, quality-gated control of polar-update exposure improves the quality–copying tradeoff relative to continued Muon training.

record.problems: The empirical study covers a limited set of architectures, datasets, and optimizer families, as the authors note. Copying results depend on the specified detector; the study says its certificate does not rule out undetected copying.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for optimizer ablations, transfer tasks, the random-feature clock tables, or checkpoint-selection comparisons: their measures are generative quality, detected copying, or theoretical clocks and do not measure any listed version.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting and held-out natural-label versus random-label accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out classifier or language-model performance under limited or broader tuning, including recovery through switching or decoupled weight decay.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipes that compensate for large batches.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error, including training-set size, excessive dropout, and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with train-test gaps, and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equal-sized random removals and measuring test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict applies to V1–V8. The omitted optimizer, transfer, clock, and selection results are declared in rows_left_out and do not establish any listed version. Theoretical spectral curvature and fluctuation clocks do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer comparisons on the listed image-classification and language benchmarks.
Large-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and batch-size effects.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to train-test error gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring held-out accuracy.

rows.subject: Muon
rows.operation_detail: Continued Muon training; common-checkpoint audit at 60k updates.
rows.measure: Observed useful interval; independent common-checkpoint copying
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± sample SD over five paired trajectories
rows.note: The interval and detected-copy rate are generative measures, not a training-test error gap.
rows.check: Table 1 values are correct; the interval is in thousands of updates. Muon is an optimizer applied to the UNet, not a model. The row bundles two measures and supplies no evidence for a listed version.

rows.subject: QGD (ours)
rows.operation_detail: Quality-gated de-whitening training; common-checkpoint audit at 60k updates.
rows.measure: Observed useful interval; independent common-checkpoint copying
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± sample SD over five paired trajectories
rows.note: The authors report an 8.32× interval expansion and 75.9% lower copying versus Muon; neither measure is the listed versions' train-test error.
rows.check: Values and Muon baseline are correct; the interval is in thousands of updates. QGD is a training controller, not a model. This own-method performance comparison belongs under fits_no_version; split the interval and copying measures if retained.
